propositions.text: The audit log is append-only: once written, an entry can never be modified or deleted through any application path, and the design makes in-place edits and out-of-order insertion structurally impossible.
Entries within a tenant are linked into a hash chain where each entry carries a prev_hash computed over the previous entry's canonical serialized content.
The first entry for a tenant chains from a fixed, well-known genesis value rather than from a real predecessor.
Altering or removing any historical entry breaks the chain for every following entry, making tampering detectable by a verifier walking from genesis.
Each tenant's entries form an independent hash chain and no entry from one tenant may appear in or be readable through another tenant's chain.
Every read and write is scoped to exactly one tenant identified by a caller-supplied tenant_id that is never inferred from the entry payload, and cross-tenant queries are disallowed.
Each entry records at minimum the actor_id, the action, the target resource, and the timestamp.
The log is queryable by actor and by inclusive time range within a single tenant, returning matching entries in ascending timestamp order.
Timestamps are stored as UTC and assigned by the subsystem at write time rather than taken from client input.
The subsystem exposes three public operations: append(tenant_id, payload), query(tenant_id, actor?, time_range?), and verify_chain(tenant_id).
verify_chain recomputes hashes along a tenant's chain and returns the position of the first tampered entry, or a no-tampering result when the chain is intact.

Retention is the only deletion path: a scheduled job deletes only whole contiguous oldest-first prefixes per tenant and records the last deleted entry's hash as the new chain anchor so the truncated chain stays verifiable.
